sentences.text: Hodie Martha cenam parat. Cena in domo Marthae est.
sentences.english: Today Martha is preparing supper. The supper is in Martha's house.

sentences.text: Anna et Lucius in domo sunt. Samuel et Marcus quoque ibi sunt.
sentences.english: Anna and Lucius are in the house. Samuel and Marcus are there too.

sentences.text: In mensa magna panis est, et lac, et vinum, et aqua. Ecce pomum et piscis!
sentences.english: On the big table there is bread, and milk, and wine, and water. Look, fruit and fish!

sentences.text: Salvete, amici! Sedete!
sentences.english: Hello, friends! Sit down!
sentences.speaker: marta

sentences.text: Salve, Martha! Gratias tibi ago. Cena bona est.
sentences.english: Hello, Martha! Thank you. The supper is good.
sentences.speaker: ana

sentences.text: Salve, Martha! Ecce, vinum tibi do.
sentences.english: Hello, Martha! Look, I give you wine.
sentences.speaker: luis

sentences.text: Gratias tibi ago, Luci! Vinum bonum est. Sedete in mensa!
sentences.english: Thank you, Lucius! The wine is good. Sit at the table!
sentences.speaker: marta

sentences.text: Omnes in mensa sedent. Martha panem omnibus dat.
sentences.english: All sit at the table. Martha gives bread to everyone.

sentences.text: Quid vultis? Panem? Lac? Piscem?
sentences.english: What do you want? Bread? Milk? Fish?
sentences.speaker: marta

sentences.text: Piscem volo! Piscis bonus est.
sentences.english: I want fish! Fish is good.
sentences.speaker: nico

sentences.text: Ego panem et pomum volo. Pomum bonum est.
sentences.english: I want bread and fruit. Fruit is good.
sentences.speaker: ana

sentences.text: Ego vinum bibo, et panem edo.
sentences.english: I drink wine, and I eat bread.
sentences.speaker: luis

sentences.text: Ego aquam bibo. Aqua mihi bona est.
sentences.english: I drink water. Water is good for me.
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: Et lac? Lacne non vis, Samuel?
sentences.english: And milk? Do you not want milk, Samuel?
sentences.speaker: marta

sentences.text: Lac quoque volo! Libenter lac bibo. Pomum quoque volo.
sentences.english: I want milk too! I gladly drink milk. I want fruit too.
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: Omnes edunt et bibunt. Cena bona est. Omnes bene valent.
sentences.english: All eat and drink. The supper is good. All are well.

sentences.text: Avia, panis tuus semper bonus est.
sentences.english: Grandmother, your bread is always good.
sentences.speaker: nico

sentences.text: Gratias tibi ago, Marce. Panem semper libenter paro. Cenam quoque libenter paro.
sentences.english: Thank you, Marcus. I always gladly make bread. I gladly make supper too.
sentences.speaker: marta

sentences.text: Anna, quomodo vales? Fessane es?
sentences.english: Anna, how are you? Are you tired?
sentences.speaker: luis

sentences.text: Fessa sum, sed bene valeo. Hodie in valetudinario laboro.
sentences.english: I am tired, but I am well. Today I work at the clinic.
sentences.speaker: ana

sentences.text: Nunc non laboras. Nunc cena est!
sentences.english: Now you are not working. Now it is supper!
sentences.speaker: luis

sentences.text: Bene! Cena bona est, et amici boni hic sunt.
sentences.english: Good! The supper is good, and good friends are here.
sentences.speaker: ana

sentences.text: Post cenam Samuel dicit: Gratias vobis ago, amici.
sentences.english: After supper Samuel says: Thank you, friends.

sentences.text: Martha dicit: Deo gratias! Pax vobis!
sentences.english: Martha says: Thanks be to God! Peace to you!

sentences.text: Omnes dicunt: Deo gratias!
sentences.english: All say: Thanks be to God!

sentences.text: Marcus fessus est. Marcus in domo dormit. Post cenam Marcus semper dormit!
sentences.english: Marcus is tired. Marcus sleeps in the house. After supper Marcus always sleeps!

sentences.text: Martha Marcum videt, et Martha bene valet. Hodie dies bonus est.
sentences.english: Martha sees Marcus, and Martha is well. Today is a good day.

sentences.text: Samuel epistulam habet. Epistula ex urbe longe venit.
sentences.english: Samuel has a letter. The letter comes from a far town.

sentences.text: Ecce epistula! Mater mea epistulam scribit. Mater cara est, et pater carus est.
sentences.english: Look, a letter! My mother is writing a letter. Mother is dear, and father is dear.
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: Quid scribit mater tua? Estne bona epistula?
sentences.english: What does your mother write? Is it a good letter?
sentences.speaker: ana

sentences.text: Bona est. Mater dicit: Bene valeo, et pater bene valet. Ubi es, Samuel? Quomodo vales?
sentences.english: It is good. Mother says: I am well, and father is well. Where are you, Samuel? How are you?
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: Mater tua bona est. Epistulam tuam libenter audio. Scribe matri tuae!
sentences.english: Your mother is good. I gladly hear your letter. Write to your mother!
sentences.speaker: marta

sentences.text: Cras matri scribo. Hodie dies bonus est, et cena bona est.
sentences.english: Tomorrow I write to my mother. Today is a good day, and the supper is good.
sentences.speaker: sam
